question: All of the following factors increases the level of respiratory neuron activity in the medulla, EXCEPT:

options.opb: Rise in H+ concentration of aerial blood

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Rise in the PCO2" -> "increased CO2 in blood" -> "stimulation of chemoreceptors" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in the medulla" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Rise in H+ concentration of arterial blood" -> "increased acidity detected by chemoreceptors" -> "stimulation of respiratory centers" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in the medulla" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Rise in Po2" -> "increased oxygen levels in blood" -> "reduced stimulation of peripheral chemoreceptors" -> "decreased respiratory neuron activity in the medulla" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Drop in Po2" -> "decreased oxygen levels in blood" -> "stimulation of peripheral chemoreceptors" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in the medulla" -> 95%
analysis: The respiratory centers in the medulla are primarily sensitive to changes in carbon dioxide (CO2) levels and hydrogen ion (H+) concentration in the blood, which reflect the acid-base status of the body. A rise in PCO2 or H+ concentration stimulates these centers to increase respiratory rate and depth to expel more CO2 and reduce acidity. Conversely, a drop in Po2 (partial pressure of oxygen) also stimulates the respiratory centers to enhance oxygen intake. However, a rise in Po2 generally does not stimulate an increase in respiratory activity, as the primary drive for breathing is CO2 levels, not oxygen levels under normal physiological conditions.
